article.intro: Watching video online is as easy as opening your phone, but a good experience does not happen by accident. This short guide covers what to keep in mind so your viewing time is more comfortable, data-friendly, and safe.

sections.title: Choose a trustworthy source
paragraphs: Start with sources whose owner is clear. Official sites and apps usually list who runs them, along with a privacy policy and terms of use. If a page gives no information about who operates it, be careful before clicking buttons or downloading anything.
Get into the habit of checking the address in your browser bar. Odd-looking addresses, long strings of numbers, or names that imitate well-known sites are often a sign that a page cannot be trusted.

sections.title: Match quality to your connection
paragraphs: HD looks sharp, but it uses far more data than standard quality. On a mobile connection, lower the resolution or turn on data saver mode so your allowance lasts longer. On stable Wi-Fi you are free to choose a higher resolution.

subsections.title: On your phone
subsections.text: Use Wi-Fi when you can, turn on data saver mode, and close other apps that consume bandwidth.

subsections.title: On your computer
subsections.text: Keep your browser up to date and disable extensions you do not need so playback runs smoothly.

sections.title: Protect your privacy and device
paragraphs: Never enter passwords, card numbers, or verification codes on a page that only offers video. Be wary of pop-ups asking you to install an app or an update, since this is a common way to spread harmful software. Install apps only from official app stores and keep your operating system up to date.

sections.title: Respect copyright and creators
paragraphs: Every video is made by someone. Watching through official channels helps creators keep making content, while redistributing it without permission can infringe copyright. If you want to share a video, share the original link and credit the source.

sections.title: Build healthy viewing habits
paragraphs: Watching for too long can strain your eyes and disrupt your sleep. Take a short break every hour, adjust screen brightness to the lighting in the room, and avoid watching right before bed. Use parental controls when children are watching too, so they only see age-appropriate content.
